pr_title: Fix #41388 by preserving protocol and port when generating routes
pr_comments: @kaspth would you mind taking a look at it? Notice that the same solution was already in place for `generate_url`, so this change was pretty much following it. I'm needing it because I use SSL in dev env and we are using direct uploads.

Cool! Though let's do our due diligence and clean the campsite while we're here:

```ruby
# For url_for_direct_upload
url_helpers.update_rails_disk_service_url(verified_token_with_expiration, default_url_options).tap do |generated_url|
  payload[:url] = generated_url
end

# For generate_url
url_helpers.rails_disk_service_url(verified_key_with_expiration, filename: filename, **default_url_options)

# Replace current_host_uri with this. No need for memoization, imo.
def default_url_options
  URI.parse(ActiveStorage::Current.host).then do |host_uri|
    { protocol: host_uri.scheme, host: host_uri.host, port: host_uri.port }
  end
end
```

@kaspth That definitively looks better! TIL about `.then` 😄 

The only thing that I'm not sure about is the name `default_url_options` since it has a special meaning, like if it's defined in a controller it will automatically affect all generated routes which is not the case here.

True, I think it's ok though. The passing is manual, but the naming still carries the same meaning: these are the default url options.

What's `Rails.application.routes.default_url_options` set to in a real Rails app, maybe we could do `Rails.application.routes.default_url_options.merge(host: ActiveStorage::Current.host)` instead?

hmm but what if the `Rails.application.routes.default_url_options` defines a different port/protocol than the value set in `ActiveStorage::Current.host` ? For example in the tests `ActiveStorage::Current.host` is set to `https://example.com` which has a protocol. It's a bit weird that it's called `host` but stores a full url though 🤔

Not liking the way we make `DiskService` parse the details it actually needs from a value that exists specifically for this purpose. How about replacing `ActiveStorage::Current.host` with `ActiveStorage::Current.url_options` or similar?

issue_context.title: Active Storage - Disk Service does not keep the host protocol in development for direct uploads
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Hi,

I was currently debugging an upload error that was only happening in development and found out that it had to do with direct uploads and the server running with SSL.

I have a file input with the option `direct_upload: true` and I'm running the server, with a self-signed SSL certificate, using the command:

```
bundle exec rails s -b 'ssl://localhost:3000?key=localhost-key.pem&cert=localhost.pem'
```

While debugging, I found out that
```ruby
url_helpers.update_rails_disk_service_url(verified_token_with_expiration, host: current_host)
```
from [this line](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/291a3d2ef29a3842d1156ada7526f4ee60dd2b59/activestorage/lib/active_storage/service/disk_service.rb#L89) is the one having the issue.

### Expected behavior

```ruby
url_helpers.update_rails_disk_service_url(verified_token_with_expiration, host: current_host)
```
should return a URL with the same protocol that `current_host` has.

### Actual behavior

```ruby
url_helpers.update_rails_disk_service_url(verified_token_with_expiration, host: current_host)
```
is returning a URL with `http` as the protocol, not keeping the `https` that `current_host` has, which in my case was `https://localhost:3000`

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.1.1

**Ruby version**: 2.6.6

### Note

This is related to the closed issue: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/40248

review_comments:
I think what @georgeclaghorn was indicating is that we also do the parsing in this class, like this:

```suggestion
  attribute :url_options

  def set_url_options_from(host)
    self.url_options = URI.parse(host).then do |uri|
      { protocol: uri.scheme, host: uri.host, port: uri.port }
    end
  end
end
```
I don’t think we need to do any parsing. We can set the right URL options based on `request` in `SetCurrent`.
